problem: If $sin⁡\theta =\frac{5}{6}$ and ${90}^{∘}<\theta <{180}^{∘}$ then what is the value of $cos⁡\theta ?$

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932638/assets/c2644fc906d4588bc39aa92d887836ff8942f5eb4b28de1baf3dc1030d2dca67.png)

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that $sin⁡\theta =\frac{1}{3},$ what is the value of $cos⁡\theta ?$
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932638/assets/4942cec8983dd2bddddd0ba2f8f9332b1b82f3999a44adb138b905457d39c633.png)

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $cos⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $sin⁡\theta =\frac{1}{3}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{1}{3})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{1}{9}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{8}{9}} \\  & =\pm \frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the negative answer since $cos⁡\theta $ is negative in the second quadrant. So, $cos⁡\theta =-\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}.$
